answer: Because the nadir calculation reruns each epoch, the voyage weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the river settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 27% independent neighbours on the funding graph. A tight ring of 29 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 31 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
